        - code: main.py

      - heading "Run your first program" [level=1]
      - paragraph: Python reads your program from the top and does each line in turn. print() shows the result.
      - text: You'll be able to
      - list:
        - listitem: → Run a program and read what it printed in the console
        - listitem: → Predict the order of the output from the order of the lines
        - listitem: → Print text, numbers and empty lines
      - text: The idea
      - paragraph: Run each example to see what it prints. Running examples doesn't count toward progress.
      - paragraph:
        - text: The examples in this course come from Runtime Market, a small online shop. An order number such as
        - code: O104839
        - text: is one order from that shop.
      - paragraph:
        - text: A Python program is a list of instructions in a file, here
        - code: main.py
        - text: . When you press Run, Python reads the file from the first line to the last and carries out each instruction in turn.
        - code: print()
        - text: is the instruction that shows something in the console.
      - text: example-1.py · Three instructions, three lines
      - button "Hide" [expanded]
      - 'button "Run again: Three instructions, three lines"': Run again
      - text: "print(\"Order O104839\") print(142.77) print(\"Status: delivered\") Order O104839 142.77 Status: delivered Three"
      - code: print
      - text: instructions, three lines of output, in the same order as the code. The middle line is the order total, a number.
      - paragraph:
        - text: Text goes inside quotes, either
        - code: "\"…\""
        - text: or
        - code: "'…'"
        - text: . The quotation marks tell Python that the characters are text. They are not printed.
        - code: print("7")
        - text: and
        - code: print(7)
        - text: both show
        - code: "7"
        - text: in the console. Numbers don't need quotes.
        - code: print()
        - text: with nothing inside prints an empty line.
      - text: example-2.py · Numbers, text and an empty line
      - 'button "Run: Numbers, text and an empty line"': Run
      - text: print("Items in cart:") print(3) print() print('Total due:') print(142.77)
